title: Ion conversation.* event stream
description: The published contract for Ion's conversation.* audit stream: one JSON object per event, delivered over any configured conversationEvents target (http, file, otel, eventhub). Full-fidelity by design — raw user text, raw assistant text, and raw tool input/output are carried unmodified. Ion performs no redaction, sanitization, or content filtering; downstream processing is the consumer's responsibility. Evolution is additive within a schema major: new optional fields may appear at any time and a consumer MUST ignore unknown ones. A breaking change bumps the `schema` value. ORDERING: events of one conversation are ordered by `ts` parsed as a timestamp (never compared as strings — RFC3339Nano trims trailing zeros, so string order is wrong), then by `payload.seq`, then by `payload.segment.part`. The engine assigns `ts` and `seq` atomically, so the two never disagree within one engine process; `seq` restarts at 1 when the engine restarts and `ts` carries the order across that boundary. SEGMENTATION: an event larger than its transport's maximum message size is delivered as several events that share every envelope field, including `event_id`, and carry `payload.segment`; see that property for reassembly.

name.description: Event type. This is the complete, frozen vocabulary of the family — a consumer may treat any other value as a schema violation.

ts.description: Event creation time, UTC, RFC3339 with nanosecond precision.

schema.description: Schema major version. Additive changes keep this value; a breaking change bumps it.

component.description: Emitting surface. Always "engine" for this family.

install_id.description: Device identity: stable per Ion installation. The key that distinguishes the same user running Ion on two machines.

event_id.description: Event identity: unique per individual event. The deduplication key for a redelivery from the durable retry queue — a replayed batch carries the same event_id it did on its first attempt. A segmented event's parts all carry the same event_id; the deduplication key is then (event_id, payload.segment.part).

user.description: User identity, from the enterprise OIDC auth context when one is present. Absent on an unauthenticated install. TRUST MODEL: this value is asserted by the client. Whatever credential the engine used to reach the configured target authorizes the transport — it proves the sender is authorized to write to the destination — but it does not attest this field. No target the engine supports propagates the authenticated sending principal to a consumer. A consumer needing verified attribution must either front the destination with a broker that validates the credential and stamps a verified claim, or reconcile this field against an independent record of the same activity.

trace_id.description: Trace identity: the W3C Trace Context trace-id (32 lowercase hex characters) of the run that produced this event, joining it to the operational OpenTelemetry trace of the same turn. Always present; empty when the event was produced outside an active traced run, so the key's presence is stable across every event.

parent_span_id.description: Span identity within the trace. Always present, on the same terms as trace_id; empty until the engine tracks a per-turn span of its own.

context.description: Correlation dimensions for this event. Keys are omitted rather than emitted empty when they do not apply.

conversation_id.description: Conversation identity: durable, and stable across application restarts, so a conversation resumed after a restart continues the same logical conversation in telemetry.

run_id.description: The run this event belongs to. Absent on events emitted outside a run.

trace_id.description: Mirrors the envelope trace_id for consumers that read correlation from the context object.

extension.description: Application context: hosting extension's friendly name. Absent when the conversation is not extension-hosted.

app_context.description: Application context supplied by the client — the surface the event came from. Keys are client-defined and the engine assigns them no meaning; the Ion desktop sends {client, tab_id}, which is what makes parallel tabs distinguishable in the stream. Absent entirely for a consumer that supplies none. A dispatched sub-agent reports its parent's value, since it runs inside the parent's surface.

payload.description: Event-specific content. See the per-event branches in allOf below.

seq.description: Per-conversation sequence number: strictly increasing across every conversation.* event of one conversation_id within one engine process, assigned in the same critical section as the envelope ts. The ordering tiebreaker after ts. Restarts at 1 when the engine restarts. Every part of a segmented event carries the same seq.

entry_id.description: Conversation-tree entry id. Absent where the backend has not minted one at emission time (delegated-CLI turns mint theirs at run exit).

dispatch_id.description: Set on every event from a dispatched sub-agent; typically absent on the root path.

extension_metadata.description: Harness-supplied envelope, returned by a before_conversation_event hook handler and carried unmodified and uninterpreted by the engine. This is where an enterprise harness attaches its own context (department, agent-pack version, dispatch chain).

segment.description: Present only on a segmented event: one whose original size exceeded the transport’s maximum message size (Event Hubs negotiates one per link) and which was therefore delivered as `parts` events sharing the same event_id. Every part carries the full envelope and every payload field; only the field named by `field` differs, holding one consecutive slice of the original value. A consumer reassembles by ordering the parts by `part`, concatenating `field` across them, and verifying the result is `total_bytes` long with the given sha256. Splits fall on UTF-8 rune boundaries, so every part is itself valid text. Engines configured with the `quarantine` oversize policy never emit this block; the oversize event is kept on the device instead.

parts.description: Total number of parts for this event_id.

field.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer, relative to payload, of the string field that was split — for example `/output` on a tool_call, or `/input/content` on a Write tool’s call.

total_bytes.description: Byte length of the original, unsplit field value.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the original, unsplit field value, for verifying reassembly.

text.description: Raw user message text, unmodified. Absent when the message carried no text.

cost.description: Per-call cost accounting. Absent — the whole key, not a zeroed object — when the backend supplied none, so "no cost reported" stays distinguishable from "cost was zero".

cost_usd.description: Computed USD cost for this call.

tool_use_id.description: Provider-assigned id for this tool invocation.

input.description: Raw tool input parameters, unmodified. Absent when the call's partial input did not parse as JSON.

output.description: Raw tool result content, unmodified. Both halves are captured: input is what the agent sent, output is what the environment returned.
